Isolated showers and thunderstorms tonight are expected to become
more scattered for Guam and Rota tonight, though more so over the
coastal waters than on land. This pattern should remain through
tomorrow morning before daytime heating and light winds allow for
scattered island effect showers and isolated thunderstorms to 
develop over Tinian and Saipan. These island effect storms will also
be possible Thursday for Tinian and Saipan. Winds appear likely to 
remain just high enough for any island effect over Guam to stay 
offshore. However, scattered monsoonal showers and isolated 
thunderstorms will remain possible. This monsoon flow is expected to 
slowly drift north throughout the week, bringing slightly higher
winds and moisture to the Marianas as soon as Thursday night. Locally
heavy showers will be possible as well but the flood risk remains
low. This monsoon pattern may then continue for the rest of the
forecast period.

Marine...
Combined seas of 6 to 7 feet tonight will decrease to about 4 to 5 
feet by Wednesday night as the west-southwesterly monsoon swell 
decreases. This may start to build back in by Friday or the weekend. 
There is a moderate risk of rip currents along North, South, and West
facing reefs for the next few days. The long period east swell is 
small enough for east facing reefs to be at low risk. There is also a
moderate risk of lightning for the next several days along the 
coastlines. Light to gentle west winds will remain for the next few 
days. An unsettled, but disorganized monsoon pattern continues to 
bring periods of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms across 
the Marianas this week with locally heavy showers possible beginning 
Friday.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Depression Atsani continues to push to the north this
afternoon with little convection noted in satellite imagery. As of
06Z, Atsani is located around 21N137E with maximum sustained winds 
at 30 mph. The current forecast from the Joint Typhoon Warning 
Center (JTWC) now dissipates Atsani as a significant tropical 
cyclone, and the final warning has been issued. For more information 
on Tropical Depression Atsani please refer to bulletins from JTWC 
under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and from the National Weather Service 
under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

JTWC opened Invest 99W this morning with a center approximated 
around 13N163E. The invest is rated sub-low by JTWC, meaning no 
development is expected over the next few days. Ensemble guidances 
suggests this disturbance will drift to the west over the next day or
so before lifting to the north.

Eastern Micronesia...
High-end scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are expected 
tonight at both Kosrae and Pohnpei with shower chances returning to
isolated or low-end scattered on Wednesday, continuing through at 
least Thursday. Mostly dry conditions are expected to prevail at 
Majuro through Friday with shower chances topping out around 30 
percent. Gentle to moderate west to southwest winds are expected to 
persist over the next couple of days at Pohnpei and Kosrae before 
easing slightly on Friday. Winds will be highest at Pohnpei with low-
end fresh winds still possible through Wednesday. Winds will be 
mostly light at Majuro through the rest of the week. Combined seas of
mostly 4 to 6 feet are expected at all three sites for the next 
several days. Seas consist of a southeast swell and a northeast 
swell. Otherwise, elevated surf will continue through the week along
south-facing reefs at both Kosrae and Majuro.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows numerous to widespread showers and scattered 
thunderstorms across Yap State and scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms across Chuuk State. Isolated showers are seen across 
Palau. Altimetry show combined seas between 6 to 8 feet across Yap 
and 4 to 7 feet across Palau and Chuuk. 

The main concern is the active monsoon pattern moving across Yap and 
Chuuk States this evening. Scattered thunderstorms have been present 
across western Yap State today with isolated thunderstorms seen 
across eastern Yap State and into Chuuk State. Over the coming days, 
this monsoon pattern looks to slowly lift northward impacting Chuuk 
through Wednesday night and Yap through Thursday. A lull in shower 
activity is expected after the active portion of the monsoon lifts 
northward. A new round of monsoonal showers and thunderstorms will 
be possible across Chuuk this weekend as the monsoon trough 
reorients itself across the region. A Special Weather Statement is 
currently in effect across Yap State for additional heavy rain this 
week that could lead to flash flooding and mudslides.

Palau looks to remain dry for the foreseeable future and drought 
concerns could grow over the coming weeks if the active monsoon 
pattern remains north of them.
